feeds.name: Threat Intelligence Feeds
feeds.description: Block domains known to distribute malware, launch phishing attacks and host command-and-control servers using a blend of the most reputable threat intelligence feeds — all updated in real time.

ai.name: AI-Driven Threat Detection
ai.description: Block millions of threats detected by our AI technology — a proprietary AI engine designed from the ground up for DNS with hundreds of signals, terabytes of training data and real-time decision making. Includes IDN homographs, typosquatting, combosquatting, DGA domains, brand impersonation, credential harvesting, malware delivery, and decoy websites used to conceal malicious infrastructure.

googleSafeBrowsing.name: Google Safe Browsing
googleSafeBrowsing.description: Block malware and phishing domains using Google Safe Browsing — a technology that examines billions of URLs per day looking for unsafe websites. Unlike the version embedded in some browsers, this does not associate your public IP address with threats and does not allow bypassing the block.

cryptojacking.name: Cryptojacking
cryptojacking.description: Prevent the unauthorized use of your devices to mine cryptocurrency.

dnsRebinding.name: DNS Rebinding
dnsRebinding.description: Prevent attackers from taking control of your local devices through the Internet by automatically blocking DNS responses containing private IP addresses.

homograph.name: IDN Homographs
homograph.description: Block internationalized domain names (IDNs) that impersonate other domains using look-alike characters — e.g., replacing the Latin letter “e” with the Cyrillic letter “е”.

typosquatting.name: Typosquatting
typosquatting.description: Block domains registered by malicious actors that target users who incorrectly type a website address into their browser — e.g., gooogle.com instead of google.com.

dga.name: Domain Generation Algorithms
dga.description: Block domains generated by Domain Generation Algorithms (DGA) and used by various families of malware as rendezvous points with their command-and-control servers.

nrd.name: Newly Registered Domains
nrd.description: Block domains registered less than 30 days ago. Those domains are known to be favored by threat actors to launch malicious campaigns.

ddns.name: Dynamic DNS Hostnames
ddns.description: Dynamic DNS (or DDNS) services let malicious actors quickly set up hostnames for free and without any validation or identity verification. While legit DDNS hostnames are rarely accessed in everyday use, their malicious counterparts are heavily used in phishing campaigns.
ddns.disclaimer: If you are using DDNS, note that this setting will not block the DDNS services' own website or their update API.

parked.name: Parked Domains
parked.description: Parked domains are single-page websites often laden with ads and devoid of any value. Parked domain monetization can expose visitors to scams, phishing pages, and malicious downloads through advertising networks and redirects.

tld.name: Top-Level Domains (TLDs)
tld.description: Block all domains and subdomains belonging to specific TLDs.

csam.name: Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)
csam.description: Block domains hosting child sexual abuse material with the help of Project Arachnid, operated by the Canadian Centre for Child Protection. No information is transmitted back to Project Arachnid when a domain is blocked.

newlyActiveDomains.name: Newly Active Domains
newlyActiveDomains.description: Block domains that are being accessed for the first time or have historically low activity. This prevents zero-day attacks and "sleeper" threats by requiring a proven footprint of legitimate usage before a domain is trusted, effectively neutralizing attempts to "pre-warm" malicious domains.

freeHostingDomains.name: Free Hosting Domains
freeHostingDomains.description: Block the default subdomains provided by free web hosting services (e.g., *.pages.dev, *.vercel.app, *.netlify.app). These "Free Hosting Domains" (FHDs) are heavily abused by attackers to host phishing sites and bypass reputation filters. This setting does not affect legitimate websites that use these providers behind a custom domain name.

tunnelingEndpoints.name: Tunneling Endpoints
tunnelingEndpoints.description: Block services that tunnel local traffic to the public internet (e.g., ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel). These tools are frequently used by attackers to bypass firewalls and host phishing pages on random subdomains while concealing their underlying infrastructure.

dataDropServices.name: Data Drop Services
dataDropServices.description: Block access to dedicated services for sharing text, files, and JSON/configuration data or collecting incoming data, including webhook requests, DNS queries, and email. This includes legitimate uses of these services.

residentialHosting.name: Residential Hosting
residentialHosting.description: Block domains that resolve to residential IP ranges (ISPs) rather than commercial data centers. Legitimate web services are rarely hosted on consumer connections, while botnet C2 servers and phishing proxies frequently run on compromised home routers.

untrustedCertificates.name: Untrusted Certificates
untrustedCertificates.description: Block domains that serve SSL/TLS certificates signed by untrusted or unknown Certificate Authorities (e.g., self-signed). While legitimate websites almost exclusively use trusted certificates, nearly 60% of commodity malware Command-and-Control (C2) servers rely on self-signed certificates or certificates issued by untrusted authorities to encrypt their traffic without leaving a paper trail.

fastFluxNetworks.name: Fast Flux Networks
fastFluxNetworks.description: Block domains that rapidly rotate their IP addresses across a distributed network of compromised devices (botnets) to evade detection. This heuristic identifies specific anomalies in DNS Time-To-Live (TTL) and IP diversity that are characteristic of malicious infrastructure and distinct from legitimate Content Delivery Networks (CDNs).

dnsDataExfiltration.name: DNS Data Exfiltration
dnsDataExfiltration.description: Block domains that use the DNS protocol to smuggle data out of your network or receive hidden commands (C2). This heuristic analyzes DNS query patterns in real time—such as abnormally long subdomains, high entropy, and unusual request types (e.g., TXT)—to detect and stop low-and-slow data theft and malware beacons (like Cobalt Strike) that evade traditional firewalls.

dnsPayloadDelivery.name: DNS Payload Delivery
dnsPayloadDelivery.description: Prevent DNS responses from being used to deliver hidden commands or payloads to your devices. Queries for record types that can carry arbitrary data but are unnecessary for everyday browsing — such as TXT or NULL — are blocked entirely. CNAME chains are flattened to their final address, removing intermediate records that could encode hidden data. For standard record types like A and AAAA, oversized answer sections are randomly truncated to corrupt any data encoded across multiple records, while preserving normal DNS functionality.

decentralizedWebGateways.name: Decentralized Web Gateways
decentralizedWebGateways.description: Block public gateways that bridge the decentralized web (e.g., IPFS) to standard browsers. Attackers heavily abuse these services to host "immutable" phishing pages and malware, allowing threats to persist by evading traditional takedowns and reputation filters.

highRiskTlds.name: High-Risk TLDs
highRiskTlds.description: Automatically block Top-Level Domains (TLDs) that are statistically dominated by malicious activity — e.g., .zip, .mov, .top. The list is updated in real time based on global abuse reputation data, protecting you from vast networks of cheap, disposable domains used for phishing and spam without requiring manual configuration.

blocklists.name: Blocklists
blocklists.description: Block ads & trackers using the most popular blocklists available — all updated in real time.

nextdns-recommended.name: NextDNS Ads & Trackers Blocklist
nextdns-recommended.description: A comprehensive blocklist to block ads & trackers in all countries. This is the recommended starter blocklist.

native.name: Native Tracking Protection
native.description: Block trackers — often operating at the operating system level — that monitor a broad range of your activity on a device. This could include all the websites you visit, everything you type or your location at all times.

disguised.name: Block Disguised Third-Party Trackers
disguised.description: Automatically detect and block third-party trackers disguising themselves as first-party to circumvent browser privacy protections like ITP.

affiliate.name: Allow Affiliate & Tracking Links
affiliate.description: Allow affiliate & tracking domains common on deals websites, in emails or in search results. Those usually only get called after manually clicking on a link.
affiliate.relay: Your IP address will automatically be hidden from those websites to preserve your privacy.

services.name: Websites, Apps & Games
services.description: Restrict access to specific websites, apps and games.
services.add: Add a website, app or game

categories.name: Categories
categories.description: Restrict access to specific categories of websites and apps.

gaming.name: Online Gaming
gaming.description: Blocks online gaming websites, online gaming apps and online gaming networks (Xbox, PlayStation Network, etc.).

piracy.name: Piracy
piracy.description: Blocks P2P websites, protocols, copyright-infringing streaming websites and generic video hosting websites used mainly for illegally distributing copyrighted content.

porn.name: Porn
porn.description: Blocks adult and pornographic content. It includes escort sites, pornhub.com and similar domains.

social-networks.name: Social Networks
social-networks.description: Blocks all social networking sites and apps (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, etc.). Does not block messaging apps.

video-streaming.name: Video Streaming
video-streaming.description: Blocks video streaming services (YouTube, Netflix, Disney+, illegal streaming websites, video porn websites, etc.) and video-based social networks (TikTok, etc.). This can also help in reducing bandwidth usage on any network.

recreation.name: Recreation Time
recreation.description: Set a period for each day of the week during which some of the websites, apps, games or categories above will not be blocked — e.g., allow Facebook on Mondays and Tuesdays between 6pm and 8pm.
recreation.howto: Use the <1></1> button in the sections above to enable Recreation Time.

safesearch.name: SafeSearch
safesearch.description: Filter explicit results on all major search engines, including images and videos. This will also block access to search engines not supporting this feature.

youtubeRestricted.name: YouTube Restricted Mode
youtubeRestricted.description: Filter out mature videos on YouTube and block embedded mature videos from being watched on other websites. This will also hide all comments.

bypass.name: Block Bypass Methods
bypass.description: Prevent or hinder the use of methods that can help bypass NextDNS filtering on the network. This includes VPNs, proxies, Tor-related software and encrypted DNS providers.

blocked.description: Domains blocked by a Security, Privacy and/or Parental Control setting or because they were manually denied.

gafam.name: GAFAM Dominance
gafam.description: The "GAFAM" (Google, Amazon, Facebook (now Meta), Apple and Microsoft) are the 5 dominant Internet companies that own many popular services, often operating under a different name, e.g., WhatsApp and Instagram for Meta.

encrypted.name: Encrypted DNS
encrypted.description: Percentage of queries made using an encrypted transport (DNS-over-HTTPS, DNS-over-TLS or the official NextDNS apps).

dnssec.name: DNSSEC
dnssec.description: Percentage of queries validated with DNSSEC.

customer_interaction.description: Includes chat, email messaging, customer support, and other interaction tools.

site_analytics.description: Collects and analyzes data related to site usage and performance.

social_media.description: Integrates features related to social media sites.

audio_video_player.description: Enables websites to publish, distribute, and optimize video and audio content.

blockpage.description: Display a block page when a domain is being blocked. This may slightly increase page load time and an HTTPS warning may appear in some cases. When disabled, blocked queries will be answered with the unspecified address (0.0.0.0 or ::).

ca.name: NextDNS Root CA
ca.description: Remove the HTTPS warning when loading the block page by installing and trusting our root CA at <1>{{link}}</1>. Read instructions on how to do this <3>here</3>.

ecs.name: Anonymized EDNS Client Subnet
ecs.description: Speed up the delivery of data from content delivery networks without exposing your IP address.

cache.name: Cache Boost
cache.description: Minimize DNS queries by enforcing a minimum TTL (Time to live).

flatten.name: CNAME Flattening
flatten.description: Prevent CNAME-chasing resolvers from making unnecessary queries and polluting the logs with intermediate domains.

ageVerification.name: Bypass Age Verification
ageVerification.description: Automatically bypass age verification checks used by certain websites, such as adult content sites, to verify a visitor’s age before allowing access.
ageVerification.acknowledgment: By enabling this feature, you acknowledge that you are legally old enough to access the content.

web3.name: Web3
web3.description: Web3 refers to a decentralized and censorship-resistant online ecosystem comprised of innovative technologies such as blockchain-based domain registries (e.g., Ethereum Name Service) and distributed content storage and delivery networks (e.g., IPFS). When enabled, NextDNS will act as an unfiltered gateway to this new Web, letting you experience it firsthand without the need to install anything.
web3.tips: As most browsers only support classic top-level domains at the moment, you should add a trailing slash ("<1>/</1>") when trying to access a Web3 domain directly (e.g., "<3>vitalik.eth/</3>" instead of "<5>vitalik.eth</5>").

rewrites.description: Set or override the DNS response for any domain. Rewrites apply to subdomains as well, and local IP addresses are supported as answers.
